comparison: Strong agreement on the key finding of parafoveal semantic integration. Both evaluate claims C7, C8, C81, C82, C84, C85, C86 as SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides detailed statistical validation (effect sizes, timing within 100ms, jackknife analysis), while peer reviewers characterize this as 'convincing evidence' and an 'important study.' Both recognize this as the central contribution.

Perfect agreement on null results during target fixation (C87, C88, C89, C119). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes this validates pre-target findings and rules out contamination, while peer reviewers implicitly accept this control analysis as part of their overall positive evaluation, noting it demonstrates specificity of parafoveal effects.

Agreement on the correlation between RIFT response and reading speed (C9, C90, C91). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides detailed statistical assessment (r=0.503, p=0.006) and notes appropriate caution about causation, while peer reviewers implicitly accept this as supporting evidence within their overall positive evaluation.

Agreement on main conclusions about parafoveal semantic integration and parallel processing (C10, C86, C130, C131, C132). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes convergent evidence and appropriate nuance in interpretation, while peer reviewers explicitly state the study provides 'convincing evidence' and 'introduces a new research paradigm.'

Agreement on eye-tracking validation (C72, C73). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides detailed statistical analysis (d=1.03) and notes consistency with prior literature, while peer reviewers treat these as standard behavioral validation measures without specific critique.

Agreement on null eye movement effect on pre-target words (C71). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes this is consistent with prior literature showing no parafoveal semantic effects in eye movements, while peer reviewers accept this as an important control showing neural effects precede behavioral manifestations.

Agreement on RIFT sensor identification and spatial characteristics (C74, C75, C76, C77, C80). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides detailed technical validation (Monte-Carlo statistics, DICS localization, spatial extent), while peer reviewers accept the technique's ability to 'separately monitor the neural processing of multiple words.'

Agreement on RIFT methodology and its advantages (C47, C50, C51, C52). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the technique is well-established through prior work and articulates its advantages, while peer reviewers explicitly state the study 'introduces a new research paradigm to the field.'

Agreement on theoretical implications for parallel processing (C102, C107, C108, C133). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the inference is justified by early timing and spatial extent, while peer reviewers characterize this as contributing 'to the understanding of how parafoveal words are neurally processed' and introducing a new paradigm.

Agreement on experimental design and methodology (C4, C5, C6, C53, C54, C55, C56, C57, C58). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides extensive detail on controls, sample size, counterbalancing, and RIFT implementation, while peer reviewers note the manuscript is 'well-written with a clear structure' and accept the methodology without specific critique.

OpenEval evaluates mechanistic explanations (C92-C97) as UNCERTAIN, noting these are speculative hypotheses (covert regression, internal attention shifts) that are plausible but not directly tested. Peer reviewers do not address these specific mechanistic claims.

OpenEval evaluates comparison to single-word processing timelines (C100, C101, C104, C106) as SUPPORTED, though noting C106 is appropriately marked as speculation. Peer reviewers do not specifically address these temporal comparison claims.

OpenEval evaluates alignment with SWIFT model and distributed attention claims (C113, C115, C116, C117, C118, C122, C123, C124) as SUPPORTED, noting some speculation is reasonable. Peer reviewers do not specifically address these model-specific theoretical alignments.

OpenEval evaluates acknowledgment of limitations (C126, C127, C128, C129) as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate scientific caution about local versus global context and correlation versus causation. Peer reviewers do not specifically discuss these limitations.
